arcs.heading: Bus routes return in stages
arcs.text: Three of the four bus routes placed on detour at the start of the week are back on their normal paths by Friday’s cutoff. A maintenance closure began the disruption; partial corridor reopening restored two routes, and a third subsequently returned. That leaves one route on detour with no return date set. The week brought substantial restoration of normal routing, but the disruption has not fully ended.

arcs.heading: A patient transfer plan takes shape
arcs.text: The clinic’s planned closure after its lease ends this month now comes with a signed agreement to transfer existing patients to two partners. The agreement gives the closure a defined transfer plan, while leaving appointment timing unsettled: current appointment dates are not guaranteed. A transfer agreement is in place; that does not establish that patients have already transferred or that their schedules will be preserved.

arcs.heading: Water notice ends within a limited scope
arcs.text: The facility-specific boil-water notice issued after filter damage ended this week following repairs and compliant samples. The change is concrete: the notice that applied during repairs and testing has been lifted. Its scope matters as much as its resolution. The clearance applies to this facility; other infrastructure was not evaluated, so the result provides no basis for a broader claim about infrastructure conditions.
